source.title: Two open problems in precedence constrained scheduling

accepted.question_text: Determine the computational complexity of the following optimization problem. There are n jobs, all available at time 0, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine. Every job has unit processing time, and each job j has an integer due date d_j. The precedence constraints are chain-like: in the directed precedence graph on the jobs, each vertex has indegree at most one and outdegree at most one, so the graph is a disjoint union of directed chains. A feasible schedule is a permutation σ of the jobs that respects the precedence constraints, meaning σ(j) < σ(k) whenever (j,k) is a precedence arc. If job j is scheduled in position σ(j), then its tardiness is T_j = max(0, σ(j) - d_j). What is the complexity of finding a precedence-feasible schedule minimizing the total tardiness Σ_j T_j?
accepted.context_brief: Single-machine unit-time scheduling with chain-like precedence constraints

accepted.question_text: Determine the computational complexity of the following optimization problem. The input is a directed precedence graph G on n unit-time jobs. The jobs must be scheduled nonpreemptively on three identical parallel machines, with at most three jobs processed in any time slot and with every precedence arc (j,k) requiring job j to be scheduled before job k. Equivalently, one seeks the minimum makespan C for which there exists a function σ from the jobs to the time slots {1, ..., C} such that σ(j) < σ(k) whenever (j,k) is an arc of G, and for every time slot t at most three jobs satisfy σ(j) = t. What is the complexity of finding this minimum makespan?
